rejectionReasons: Current Kick History advertises custom ranges up to 90 days and computes a previous-period comparison as part of the existing derived History contract.
Exact observation-time Kick category membership exists in retained raw snapshots, but those minute_snapshots are deleted after 60 days.
The 180-day daily_rollups that support long-range History do not preserve category identity or selected-category contribution in top_streamers_json.

A 90-day selected-category current period cannot be reconstructed exactly after the oldest 30 days have left raw retention; its previous-period comparison can require category-aware history across up to 180 days.

Using latest category state, synthetic/name-only mapping, zero-filling unavailable category history, hidden backfill, retention expansion, or provider mixing would change the accepted data semantics and is not authorized by this decision.
futureReconsiderationRequirements: Introduce a separately governed History-grade Kick category aggregate that preserves every selected-category contribution before category-specific ranking or capping.
Retain category-aware History data long enough to cover the advertised current period plus the full previous-period comparison window.
Preserve provider-scoped observation-time category identity rather than projecting a latest category state backward.
Expose explicit category coverage and missing-data metadata and never coerce unavailable category history to zero.
Accumulate any new History-grade category data forward; do not create a hidden historical backfill under this decision.
nextGate: No Kick History category runtime, API parameter, hidden candidate, or UI. A separate data/storage decision is required before reconsideration.
